newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says Exxon wins Timan oil tender.
newsitem.headline: Russia says Exxon wins Timan oil tender.

text.p: Exxon Corp. has won a tender to explore and develop Russian oil fields in Central-Khoreiverskaya in the northern Timan-Pechora region, a senior regional official said Thursday.

"We selected Exxon this morning," said Anatoly Kazakov, deputy head of the Arkhangelsk regional administration and head of the region's natural resources department, in a telephone interview from Arkhangelsk, the city that handled the tender.
Under the terms of the tender, Exxon would develop the fields on a production-sharing basis and would have a 50 percent stake in the project.
Russian oil companies Rosneft, KomiTEK and exploration outfit Arkhangelskgeoldobycha would split equally the remaining 50 percent stake, he said.
He said the contract zone covers 2,261 square km (904.4 square miles) and that crude oil reserves there were 156-165 million metric tons.
Officials have said the production-sharing deal will cost several billion dollars.

Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin said last month that Moscow had planned to ask the other bidders in the tender -- named as Amoco Corp., Texaco Inc., Total SA of France and Norsk Hydro ASA -- to form a consortium to tap the reserves.
Kazakov declined to say what had happened to the consortium idea and Rosneft officials were unable to comment.
Interfax news agency said an early feasibility study presented by Exxon saw production drilling beginning in 2001, but the agency said KomiTEK had sought to begin in 1999.
Kazakov said the Russian parliament had agreed to include the Khoreiverskaya reserves on its list of fields open to production-sharing agreements. The list has yet to be approved.
